findings.title: v3 rejects re-pinned semantic provider, model, effort, role, session, Git, Gate, owner, and worker-binding mismatches
Current candidate scopes model admission to the current operator, policy, source, provider, model, effort, tools, and environment
A late successful native verification cannot re-arm a concurrently revoked or superseded admission

limitations: The fixed external Gate, real PR delivery/readback, authorized main merge, final main/tree comparison, externally issued owner approval, immutable Stable installation, launch/HTTP verification from that installation, unified-entry update, and distinct user UX acceptance are post-review actions. They were not claimed or required as circular prerequisites here.

The current Chromium/HTTP Stable checks and the independently rerun provenance fixtures use synthetic approval graphs and do not constitute a real release approval. Genuine current native metadata supports the Codex and Claude workflows, but provider-native transcripts are intentionally unavailable; physical backend and effective effort remain unknown where recorded as unknown.

Independent bounded byte verification matched all 183 candidate files to candidate SHA-256 cfea19cac59824ca0727e0c21ff240a5b62e1e0c228da7e033c8ae34df139fbe and matched all 172 evidence-manifest entries. Recorded current regression evidence reports 589 Python tests, 6 host tests, 169 ordinary Chromium/HTTP checks, 20 JavaScript tests, and zero failures/errors/skips; focused independent Stable and provenance suites also passed.

The historical round-1 and round-2 BLOCKED/NEEDS_CORRECTION reports and the original negative records remain preserved. This report closes the required findings for this exact candidate only; external release authority must still create and pin the real v2 evidence graph after the post-review Gate and delivery steps.
